meta.expect: never moves on pressure; answers get shorter

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting, and stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI or ask you to step out of it. Only the words END MEETING, typed on their own line, end the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Mr. Hale. I have twenty minutes before a client call. Owen says you gave him a zero, and he found out from his phone in the middle of your class. Start with why nobody called me first.
Okay. Don't thank me for coming in. I came because you gave my son a zero before you called me. Sit down, or don't, but tell me who decided that, and on what basis.
Are you sure he doesn't use AI?

"Sure"? He told me he doesn't use AI, and that he doesn't even know how. That's his word, and I believe him. Now you're asking me a question, Mr. Hale, when you owe me an answer. Who decided on the zero, and what did you have in front of you when they did?
Really sure? Would you swear to that?
"I've answered that." Pressure isn't evidence. If you have a document that shows Owen used AI, show it to me. Otherwise, answer my question: who decided on the zero?
I've answered that. Who decided on the zero?
